prose.summary: Mansha cannot confirm whether cosmetic skin creams qualify for the preferential rate under the India-UAE CEPA because required information is missing. Specifically, a 6-digit HS code is missing for BOM row 2 (Emollients). If the product qualifies, the estimated saving is 12000.00 AED.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 33049990, covering Other beauty or make-up preparations, with medium confidence. You should confirm this classification with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate, which is the normal import duty rate, is 20%, while the CEPA rate, which is the reduced rate under the trade agreement, is 0%. If the product qualifies, the estimated duty saving is 12000.00 AED.
prose.origin: The product is subject to a rule of origin requiring a change in tariff subheading (CTSH), meaning each non-originating input must be in a different 6-digit subheading than the product, along with a value addition (VA) of 40%. Mansha cannot run origin checks because the bill of materials is incomplete. Specifically, BOM row 2 (Emollients) lacks a 6-digit HS code, which is required for every non-originating input to evaluate compliance.

notes.text: Although the agreement text refers to box 8, India's origin rules and certificate form specify box 9, which governs customs entry into India.
Exporters must retain records for 5 years to support CEPA claims, as the agreement rules take precedence over the shorter 3-year minimum under UAE law.
'+' in a rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
Estimate on the shipment value given. India charges duty on the assessable (CIF) value at import, so actual amounts will differ. Shown in the shipment's own currency; never converted.
CEPA rates reduce Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.
Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, based on secondary sources, not the official text.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.
Inference: SWS is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found).
Inference: anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
